title: Collabstr Alternatives for UGC Creators (2026): Fees, Who Can Join and Payouts
excerpt: The best Collabstr alternatives for UGC creators in 2026, compared from each platform's own pages: fees taken from your pay, who can join, how you get work and how you get paid.

content:
Collabstr is free to join but keeps 15% of every order, and you mostly wait for brands to buy your packages. If you want a smaller cut, a different way of finding work, or a platform that accepts creators in your country, these are the alternatives worth knowing in 2026.

Disclosure: Newcollab is also a platform for UGC creators. We only state what the other platforms publish on their own pricing, FAQ and help pages, link the source for each fact, and describe our own product in the same way. We checked every page in November 2026; fees change, so confirm on the platform before you sign up.

Platform by platform

JoinBrands

A marketplace where brands post UGC jobs at fixed prices and creators apply. Free to join for creators 18+ in the US, UK, Germany, Australia or Canada, with no follower requirement, but you pass a short free certification for each content type first. The free plan keeps 20% of your pay; Creator PRO ($49.95 a month) lowers that to 15%. Brands often send the product, which you keep. (joinbrands.com/creator)

Billo

A managed UGC video marketplace: brands buy videos, approved creators pick up the tasks. No follower requirement; you apply with a short video pitch that Billo reviews within about a week. Billo publishes its own pay figures: a 15-second video starts at $30 for new creators and $70 at Premium level, which unlocks after 14 videos. (billo.app/for-creators)

Insense

A brand-side platform with a free creator app where you apply to paid campaigns. It is stricter on entry: at least 1,000 Instagram followers or a median of 500 TikTok views, 1%+ engagement and a UGC portfolio. Its creator terms mention payouts "less any applicable service fees", without a published rate. (insense.pro/faq)

Upfluence

Mostly brand software, with a free creator marketplace where you apply to brand deals. It says creators keep 100% and pay no subscription or listing fee, and it welcomes nano and micro creators. (upfluence.com)

Aspire

A brand-side platform with a creator marketplace. Aspire says it is free for creators and never takes a percentage of your deal. Paid campaigns have follower and engagement thresholds; creators under 5K followers are pointed to its Maven app, which is mostly product seeding and UGC. (aspire.io/influencers)

Influee

Closest to Collabstr's model: you set your own rates and brands hire you. The difference is the fee: Influee adds its 10% on top of the brand's price instead of taking it from yours. (influee.co/for-creators)

#paid

Better for creators who already have an audience: it typically looks for 10,000+ followers and 1.5%+ engagement. You set your own rates, and every deal includes 12 months of owned-channel rights for the brand. Payment follows a 30-day processing cycle. (hashtagpaid.com/creators)

Trend (now part of soona)

Trend was acquired by soona, and its creator applications now point to soona, with Trend campaigns supported through the end of 2026. It has been US-only and iPhone-only, so check soona's current creator page before you apply. (soona.co)

Newcollab

Not a marketplace you wait in. Newcollab lists the PR contact or application form for 3,000+ brands, a feed of paid UGC gigs, and your free UGC portfolio. On Pro ($19 a month), Polly, its AI agent, finds brands that fit your niche and pitches them from your own Gmail, with follow-ups. Brands pay you directly and Newcollab takes no commission. The free plan includes 3 brand applications a month and has no follower minimum.

How to choose

  • No followers yet: Billo, JoinBrands, Upfluence, Influee and Newcollab state no follower minimum.
  • Keep the most of each deal: Upfluence, Aspire, Influee and Newcollab take nothing from creator pay.
  • Outside the US: check country rules first. Billo and JoinBrands only accept a few countries.
  • Set your own prices: Collabstr, Influee and #paid let you set rates; JoinBrands and Billo use fixed prices.
  • Use more than one: most working UGC creators combine a platform or two with pitching brands directly. Start with what to charge for UGC.

faq.question: What is the best Collabstr alternative for beginners?
faq.answer: One that accepts creators with no followers in your country. Billo, JoinBrands, Upfluence and Influee state no follower minimum; Billo and JoinBrands only accept a few countries.

faq.question: Which Collabstr alternatives take no commission from creators?
faq.answer: Upfluence says creators keep 100%, Aspire says it never takes a percentage, Influee charges its 10% fee to the brand, and Newcollab charges no commission. Collabstr keeps 15% and JoinBrands 20% (15% with Creator PRO).

faq.question: Is Collabstr better than JoinBrands?
faq.answer: It depends on how you want to work. On Collabstr you set your own package prices and brands buy them, minus a 15% fee. On JoinBrands you apply to fixed-price jobs, minus a 20% fee (15% with Creator PRO), and you need to live in one of five countries.

faq.question: Can I use Collabstr and other platforms at the same time?
faq.answer: Yes. None of the platforms here require exclusivity to join, and most UGC creators combine a platform or two with pitching brands directly.
